name: Big Society
summary: Big Society was the British Conservative-led coalition's 2010 programme to shift power and responsibility from Whitehall to neighbourhoods, volunteers, charities, co-operatives and social enterprises. It paired civic-conservative communitarianism with free-market economics, opening public services to non-state providers and promoting volunteering, philanthropy and open government data. Critics saw it as cover for spending cuts; supporters said it predated them.
scope: The programme as launched by David Cameron and Nick Clegg in May and July 2010 (drawing on Steve Hilton's and David Willetts's civic conservatism), including the Localism Act 2011, National Citizen Service, Big Society Capital and community rights. It covers the 2010-2015 policy agenda and excludes the later participation-society variants abroad. Few general political questions are answered by sources, so most answers are inferences.

sources.title: PM and Deputy PM's speeches at Big Society launch
sources.author: David Cameron and Nick Clegg
sources.usedFor: Coalition framing, community right to buy, National Citizen Service, open data.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not part of the programme; the 2010 coalition kept the NHS, and Cameron's government framed Big Society as reform of delivery, so tax-funded universal care is assumed as the settled baseline.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Big Society sources never address wage floors; Conservative and Liberal Democrat adherents were split on large rises.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The speech opens public services to private companies and social enterprises and pairs free-market economics with civic conservatism, though it denies markets alone suffice.

public-ownership.rationale: Big Society favoured transferring assets and services to community groups, co-ops and private providers rather than state ownership of utilities; inferred, never stated for energy and rail.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Wikipedia account notes a 2012 cap on charity tax relief drew criticism but no sources show a push for higher wealth taxes; the programme relied on philanthropy by the wealthy instead.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not discussed; Big Society praises civic associations generally but sat in a Conservative-led coalition cutting public-sector budgets.

property-fundamental.rationale: Community rights to buy assets of community value gave localities limited power over private property, but the sources never frame property as an absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Programme stressed freeing providers from central bureaucracy; inferred that adherents favoured lighter central control, though not hostile to regulation as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cameron criticised state help for making people passive recipients, yet the speech proposes no welfare cuts; Cameron-era critics tied cuts to Big Society while supporters denied it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Co-ops, mutuals and employee-owned public service spin-outs were explicitly encouraged, but collective worker ownership as a general rule was not a goal.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Counter-terrorism surveillance is outside the programme; open-data transparency of government was a theme but says nothing on surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cameron's launch speech lists drug abuse as a social problem for communities and charities to tackle; no case for legalisation appears.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed in any Big Society source.

strong-leader.rationale: The speech rejects top-down micromanagement from Westminster and promises to push power to the person on the street, which cuts against a leader bypassing gridlock.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is outside the programme and UK firearms law was not touched by it; adherents are split in the coalition tradition.

empower-police-military.rationale: The programme was linked to public spending cuts and community crime maps; no source calls for more police or military authority.

state-harmful.rationale: Big Society wants a government that enables civil society, not abolition; Cameron said government must help build it, so the state is judged necessary.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex-work law is never discussed; Conservative and Liberal Democrat adherents hold conscience views, so no position is inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Cameron called for the biggest redistribution of power from Whitehall to the man and woman on the street and said it should be driven down into communities; the Localism Act 2011 enacted it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Prison purpose is not addressed; the nearest link is charities and social enterprises delivering offender services, which suggests no firm stance.

traditional-family.rationale: Civic conservatism leans toward family and community as social foundations, but the Big Society sources stress neighbourhoods and associations rather than family form.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The coalition legalised it in 2013 under Cameron, and Clegg's Liberalism-equals-Big-Society framing suggests tolerance; Big Society itself never addressed it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion was a conscience matter in both coalition parties and the programme never touched it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Faith groups were welcome as community partners but no source seeks a larger religious public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Cameron's launch speeches name poverty and disadvantage but never historical racial redress, so no position can be inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A philosophical question about gender that no Big Society source takes up.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Civic conservatism values tradition, but Big Society focused on neighbourhood action rather than national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Civic conservative roots favour working through existing institutions and voluntary reform, yet the speech calls for a dramatic power shift; inferred as mildly gradualist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not part of Big Society; it was a separate coalition debate.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The programme is domestic and localist; inferred scepticism toward distant, centralised authority.

free-trade.rationale: Pro-market Conservative orientation suggests support, but trade is not mentioned in Big Society sources.

nation-first.rationale: The programme is domestic and localist and says nothing about global cooperation versus national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is outside Big Society, which is about domestic civil society.

open-borders.rationale: Nothing on borders; the neighbourhood-community emphasis and mainstream Conservative position imply rejection.

limit-growth.rationale: Programme was paired with free-market economics and deficit-led recovery; no sign of degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy was handled elsewhere by the coalition; Big Society sources are silent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Open government data and crime maps were treated as empowering tools, but no claim that technology solves most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is not part of the programme.

revolution-justified.rationale: The speech seeks a peaceful cultural shift via citizens and government; Clegg called it a huge cultural shift, not rupture.

experts-over-public.rationale: Speech faults top-down bureaucracy and says solutions should come from communities not officials, while giving professionals more freedom; so experts should not override public voice.

central-planning.rationale: Cameron attacked centralised micromanagement that he said does not work, and favoured markets and diverse providers.

socialized-markets.rationale: Co-ops and mutuals were backed alongside private firms; no sources say that only worker- or public-owned firms make markets acceptable.

land-value-tax.rationale: No Big Society source discusses land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not covered; a Conservative-led government favouring philanthropy and lower taxes would lean against heavy inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Speech criticised passive dependency on state help and favoured active participation; unconditional income inferred as disfavoured.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not covered; the pro-market side of Big Society implies mild scepticism of protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state's role is to enable social investment (Big Society Capital drew on bank funds and dormant accounts) rather than to direct strategic industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Community asset ownership and right-to-buy for pubs and post offices spread ownership to groups, an approximate fit; not an explicit property doctrine.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed; mainstream Conservative and Liberal Democrat adherents backed the Bank of England.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not discussed; compulsory state-recognised wage bodies sit badly with a voluntary, bottom-up programme.

one-party-rule.rationale: Big Society was launched by a coalition and through pluralist civil society, in line with liberal-democratic politics.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: UK adherents worked within the constitutional monarchy; Big Society itself was silent.

democracy-best.rationale: Programme aims to deepen democratic participation; the sources say nothing on voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Localism Act added referendum powers and community rights, but no source says citizens should replace representatives.

workers-councils.rationale: Programme works through local councils, charities and voluntary bodies, not workers' councils as organs of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programme devolves to neighbourhoods inside the UK; secession is never raised.

natural-rulers.rationale: Speech emphasises ordinary citizens' power against elites in Whitehall.

political-violence-never.rationale: Never discussed, but a programme resting on voluntary civic action implies rejecting violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Cameron's youth scheme builds character through voluntary service, so war is unlikely to be endorsed; never discussed.

separate-church-state.rationale: Faith groups were welcomed as partners; formal church-state relations are not addressed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Programme is secular-civic; faith groups participate as voluntary partners only.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private provision was proposed for social services, not for courts or defence; inferred rejection.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence strategy is outside the programme.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Big Society is framed around local neighbourhoods open to all residents; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Programme assumes cooperation between citizens, charities, business and state, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Aim was tackling poverty and empowering communities, not equalising outcomes; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not relevant to the English programme, so no position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Never discussed by any Big Society source.

civilizational-union.rationale: The programme is local; supranational civilisational blocs are not discussed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The programme asks people to give time and money to community; Cameron's launch speech rests on responsibility rather than self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Clegg paired Empowerment with Responsibility, and the speech asks citizens to give time and money; duties to community are stressed without ranking them over rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics are not part of Big Society.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is never discussed; coercive limits conflict with liberal voluntarism.

conscription.rationale: Voluntary service was the model: National Citizen Service is a voluntary programme for 16- and 17-year-olds.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme stresses civic voice and participation in communities, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Cameron opened services to private providers and wanted a leaner state, but the programme frames citizens as participants, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Speech wants people free and powerful enough to help themselves, which partly echoes empowerment, but no stated doctrine on material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source discusses media or universities as political powers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not part of the programme, and Clegg and Cameron's coalition rejected race science; inferred from mainstream centre-right and liberal values.

organic-representation.rationale: Programme gives power to local communities and associations, partially echoing it, but representation through families is never proposed.

total-state.rationale: The ideology's premise is that the state should shrink back and let civil society act.

national-rebirth.rationale: Big Society is incremental reform of civic life, not national regeneration; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority is by election and law in the programme; personal loyalty oaths have no place.

bound-labor.rationale: Programme is voluntarist and liberal, opposing compulsory service or bondage.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: An epistemological claim that Big Society never touches.

universal-morality.rationale: Civic conservatism leans toward shared moral standards, but the sources never state a view on universal morality.

single-common-good.rationale: Big Society speaks of the common good in terms of community, but also values plural civic associations.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Foreign and national-question issue outside the programme.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Programme is domestic and no source discusses diaspora return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: No source discusses language revival; the programme's localism concerns services and civic power.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mutuals and employee-led spin-outs were encouraged, but democratic control of large companies was not a programme aim.

school-vouchers.rationale: Free schools under the Academies Act 2010 let parents, charities and businesses run schools, which fits choice, but vouchers were not adopted.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Cameron presented Big Society as a complement to deficit reduction, accepting hard spending decisions as in the national interest.

economic-freedom.rationale: The programme mixes market economics with social obligation; no statement about political freedom depending on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not discussed; the speech relies on citizens' initiative more than rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The programme's devolution is inside the UK, so no stance on national self-determination appears.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign policy is outside the programme.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not discussed; faith groups were treated as welcome partners.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is not discussed in the sources.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Speech criticised passivity in state help and favoured participation; work conditions are an inference, since the sources say nothing on benefit rules.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cameron and Clegg frame cooperation between citizens, business, charities and state as the method; Cameron backs the voluntary sector leading change, not conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; the community right to buy sought to keep pubs and post offices in local hands, implying heritage institutions are saved by communities.

dominated-front.rationale: A question about countries dominated by Western powers has no bearing on this domestic programme.

workers-nation.rationale: Organising the working class nationally or internationally is irrelevant to a programme built on cross-class cooperation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not discussed; coalition adherents favoured equal legal treatment.

ban-interest.rationale: Big Society Capital worked with banks and social investment, relying on interest-bearing finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposed by the liberal-conservative coalition values behind the programme; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Programme treats the state as an enabler of civil society, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not part of the programme.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Integration is not discussed in the sources, though the programme aims at local cohesion.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in any Big Society source; adherents sit within mainstream politics.

proportional-representation.rationale: Clegg's party wanted it but Cameron's did not; the coalition held an AV referendum instead, so adherents split.

national-mission.rationale: Not discussed; the programme is domestic.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: A sociological claim that Big Society never addresses.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Speech attacks Whitehall elites and wasteful bureaucracy but not as corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not part of the programme and conflicts with its voluntarist liberal base; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice is outside the programme.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The speech wants a government that helps build the Big Society and funds social programmes, not one limited to defence and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the programme; inferred rejection from its liberal-communitarian framing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Clegg's liberal reading implies equal worth; not specifically discussed.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no bearing on Big Society.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Colonial history of settler states is never addressed in Big Society sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not discussed; a question about personal law that the programme does not raise.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious and animal-slaughter laws are untouched by the programme.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Free schools included faith groups; no stance on state school religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea at odds with the programme's aim of rebalancing power away from the state.

population-transfer.rationale: Not part of the programme; inferred rejection from liberal values.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian principle never stated in Big Society sources.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Programme opens services to competing providers but speaks of cooperation, not struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banning parties is not discussed; the programme is pluralist but silent on it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican philosophical claim the sources never address.

separated-powers.rationale: Programme assumes a constitutional liberal order and dispersal of power; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Programme begins from citizens' own initiative rather than leadership by a party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Cameron cites tackling entrenched poverty and disadvantaged children as goals; the sources do not set priority rules.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Mainstream Conservative policy and consistent with spreading ownership; not in Big Society sources, which mention community right to buy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations are not discussed; the sources are silent.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not discussed; Cameron attributes poverty to entrenched social problems, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not discussed; the programme aims to build neighbourhood cohesion in existing communities, suggesting rejection.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not proposed in any source; offices stay elective in the programme.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are outside the programme's domestic civic focus.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not discussed; market orientation implies mild rejection.

party-controls-media.rationale: Programme favours open government and transparency.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the programme sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of politicians is not addressed; the programme has no stance on representatives' pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not addressed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not discussed; localism suggests wariness of distant bodies, though the coalition was pro-EU membership.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Command of the armed forces is a constitutional matter the programme does not address.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not addressed; the programme treats faith groups as voluntary partners.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Great-power war strategy is irrelevant to the programme.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not discussed; liberal-conservative adherents would not endorse state censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Election-term rules are not discussed in the sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Localism Act gave communities new powers over councils; recall is not specifically mentioned.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not discussed; the coalition kept NATO membership.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Programme has no such goal; relies on market and community mix.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural versus urban morality is never mentioned; the vanguard areas included both city and country.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not applicable to the UK programme.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not discussed, though the speech faults Whitehall elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not discussed in the sources.

death-penalty.rationale: Not discussed; mainstream Conservative leaders did not pursue it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curriculum content is not addressed; free schools got freedom over it only indirectly.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; free schools raised the issue indirectly but the programme took no stance.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Content regulation is not addressed by any source.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not part of the programme.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is not part of the programme.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemption from general laws is not discussed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; civic conservatism may favour conformity to community norms but no source says so.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not discussed; deficit-reducing Conservatives would resist debt cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial question with no bearing here.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is not discussed, though localist reform was done by statute.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The programme seeks to widen citizens' freedom to act, so restricting freedoms is inferred as unwelcome.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not discussed; the Big Society speeches concern domestic giving.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not discussed, though the Conservative-led coalition kept Trident.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Head of state selection is not discussed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not discussed; the coalition kept an independent Bank of England.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial disputes are outside the programme.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property theory is not discussed; the programme treats ownership as compatible with community ownership.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Historical debate irrelevant to Big Society.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: Not discussed; coalition stayed in NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International law on annexation is outside the programme.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not discussed; faith groups were welcomed as community partners, implying no curbing.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; the monarchy was left undisturbed by the programme.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is never raised, and devolution stays inside the UK.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional integration deals are not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not discussed, though the programme assumes communities shape people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not part of the programme; adherents operate in a constitutional democracy.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not part of the programme.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed in the sources.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court policy is not addressed by the programme.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist-Leninist idea with no bearing on Big Society.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not part of the programme; community asset ownership is not confiscation.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee policy is outside this domestic programme.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed; Conservatives in the coalition opposed the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic union is irrelevant to the programme.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural institutions are not discussed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy is not discussed in the sources.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not mentioned in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not discussed; the coalition had just inherited the 2008 bank rescues.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial constraint on majorities is not discussed.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quota rules are not discussed in the programme.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is not discussed; the programme works within an open market economy.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement content is outside the programme.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; Big Society leans on voluntary giving but also on financial instruments like Big Society Capital.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not discussed; coalition did pursue Lords reform separately.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School history teaching is not discussed.

patriotic-education.rationale: National Citizen Service fosters civic participation but not nationalism as such.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions policy is not discussed by Big Society sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not discussed; Big Society Capital used bank funds and dormant accounts.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not discussed, though Big Society assumes a market economy that persists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anti-discrimination law is not discussed in the sources.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights design is not discussed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial boundaries are outside the programme.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not discussed; implied by operating within a representative democracy.

minority-veto.rationale: Unanimity rules are not discussed; localism favours community decision-making but not individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rights of resistance are not discussed; programme works within constitutional order.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not discussed; implied by Westminster constitutional practice.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The speech and Cameron's emphasis on philanthropy ask the wealthy to give time and money to others; it is the voluntary version of this duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The programme asks citizens to become active in community life, the opposite of withdrawal.

native-born-offices.rationale: Office eligibility rules are not discussed.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous political representation is not relevant to the programme.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional founding values are not discussed.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American historical debate has no bearing on Big Society.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not discussed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender disadvantage policy is not discussed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence debate is not addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Universality of Western institutions is not discussed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not part of the programme; adherents accept civilian control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognising unpaid care is not discussed, though volunteering was valued as unpaid work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not discussed, though civic conservatism values family obligation.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign investment screening is not discussed; open-market orientation suggests mild opposition.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates are not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not discussed; community ownership of local assets is limited and individual tenure is assumed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not discussed; implied by Westminster practice.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership rules for foreigners are not addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture is not discussed; the programme asks citizens to give time and money but does not criticise consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is outside the programme.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying is not discussed in the sources, though the programme invited corporate partners.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: NGO funding restrictions are not discussed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; localism did not extend to residents-only purchasing.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not discussed; the speech's criticism of passive state dependence implies reluctance.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is not addressed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not discussed; the programme assumes civic responsibility.

non-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is outside the programme.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; coalition legislated on marriage, not abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Open data and transparency were one of five core launch policies; Cameron cited crime maps and open government data as tools for citizens.

local-production.rationale: Not discussed, though localism concerns decision power more than production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not discussed, though informal neighbourhood action is welcomed.

religious-nation.rationale: National identity by religion is not discussed.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not discussed; localism pushes powers but the sources never mention revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Socialist property distinction is irrelevant to a market-based programme.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War strategy is not discussed.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The speech opens services to charities, social enterprises and private firms, and up to 25 percent of contracts were planned to move to non-state providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not discussed; faith groups are valued participants.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Historical judgement of capitalism is not discussed, though the programme assumes it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Feminist economic analysis is not discussed in sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; Big Society leans toward care by families and community groups, not public service.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Co-ops, mutuals and neighbourhood groups were promoted, though not as a total reorganisation of society.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not discussed; Big Society sits within market capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Territorial claims are outside the programme.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not part of the programme; the coalition legalised same-sex marriage.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic jurisprudence is outside the programme.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Core claim: communities and citizens should take decisions directly and share responsibility; the 2010 launch aims to give them rights to bid for services and assets.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is not discussed in sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender recognition law is not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Clegg described Liberalism and Big Society as different words for one idea, suggesting cross-party framing, but the programme remained within the party system.

social-market-economy.rationale: Civic conservatism combines markets with social obligation through community; Cameron's launch speech wanted markets and community together.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succession in office is not discussed, beyond the UK monarchy being unchanged.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not discussed; Big Society Capital worked through conventional finance.

online-participation.rationale: Open data and tools for citizens suggest support; inference only.

open-government-data.rationale: Publishing government data for open government was a core launch commitment; Cameron cited crime maps and data publication.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed, though deliberative engagement fits the participatory spirit.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not discussed as a liberty problem, though critics noted Big Society favoured big charities.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military personnel policy is not discussed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The programme gave charities and communities a bigger role in helping the poor, though Cameron said government should still help build it; critics saw it as shifting duty away from the state.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office rules are not discussed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Local voting rights for foreigners are not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Not discussed; market orientation suggests rejection.

uniformed-youth.rationale: National Citizen Service is a state-backed youth programme but is civic and voluntary, not uniformed drilling.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Historical recognition policy is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Distribution theory is not discussed; private and investment returns are accepted by the programme.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National origin myths are not discussed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Boundary design for peoples is not discussed.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Programme moves local services toward mixed providers and community ownership rather than public ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: Parliament structure is not discussed in sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Community assets owned by local groups fit partly, but local-government ownership of production was not a goal.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Municipal confederation is not discussed, though localism is neighbouring.

family-wage.rationale: Wage norms are not discussed, though civic conservatism values family.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Medical research funding is not discussed.

person-over-state.rationale: Programme puts citizens ahead of Whitehall; the speech asks for solutions from people not officials.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Anthropology of the person is not discussed.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Whether devolved powers can be withdrawn is not discussed; Localism Act gave statutory rights to communities.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial identity politics is not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Use of force is not discussed.

communal-electorates.rationale: Electoral design by religion is not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy theory with no basis in sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; the coalition raised tuition fees.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Big Society is built on markets, social investment and charitable funding, none of which fits abolishing money and wages.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme assumes an advanced market economy, uses banks' capital for social investment, and speaks of growth and recovery.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Open data and crime maps were promoted, but nothing in the sources argues for speeding disruptive change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics is untouched by the programme.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Programme moves decisions toward citizens and neighbourhoods, which cuts against handing them to algorithms; never discussed.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not addressed in any source.

restore-past-order.rationale: Civic conservatism values tradition, but the launch speeches call for a dramatic new power shift, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cameron said centralised management simply does not work and the programme was presented pragmatically; no source states the principle.

direct-action.rationale: Change is sought through government programmes and legislation like the Localism Act 2011 plus voluntary action, not against parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: Programme wants social change delivered through voluntary participation, so means resemble the aim; inferred from the speeches.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The programme assumes a developed economy and has no primitivist element.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Programme relies on specialist charities, firms and professionals, giving professionals more freedom.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not a stated aim; the programme mixes state, market and charity and never proposes need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: Private and social-enterprise providers are welcomed to deliver services, so profit-making stays acceptable.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programme welcomes private companies and bank capital as partners, treating profit as legitimate.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Programme is democratic and cooperative, with no class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Never discussed; community ownership applies to local assets like pubs, not farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Programme works within market capitalism and the sources contain no such theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: Programme is funded by government and relies on state budgets and lottery money, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Not discussed; civic conservatism is more willing to endorse moral expectations than a pure harm rule.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Programme emphasises communities, neighbourhood groups and duties as well as individuals; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The programme sources never address environmental taxation; coalition partners and Conservative adherents were split between market-based tools and regulation.

future-generations.rationale: Not a stated pillar; civic-conservative communitarianism stresses duties to community and inheritance, so a duty to those who come after is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The programme never framed women as bringing distinct values; its volunteering and community emphasis is gender-neutral, so the claim is inferred to be rejected by a typical adherent.

arms-reduction.rationale: Defence policy lay outside the Big Society programme and the coalition kept a strong defence stance, so no position is stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The programme's openness concerned government data and transparency at home, not treaties; nothing is stated on diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: The programme paired civic action with free-market economics and the coalition kept open capital markets, so state control of capital movement is inferred to be rejected.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative and Liberal Democrat support for state security forces; the sources do not discuss private arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The coalition government fought wars and kept the armed forces as a central duty, so refusal runs against the programme.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; Conservatives and Liberal Democrats were split on union bargaining, and the programme stresses voluntary action.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The coalition kept tax credits and reformed them toward Universal Credit, which top up low-paid workers' pay.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Cameron and Clegg's government set the Office for Budget Responsibility and fiscal targets, which the sources link to austerity.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not part of the programme; coalition members were divided and the sources do not address trade rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Cameron's speech aims to give power to communities through existing institutions and reform of the state, not to dismantle it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The programme favours voluntary groups, co-operatives and social enterprises alongside markets; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not part of the programme; the coalition pursued natural capital work, but adherents are not clearly split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cameron's civic conservatism values community but is liberal and pluralist rather than treating the nation as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the coalition's austerity and fiscal restraint; the sources do not discuss student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the localist, unitary-state outlook of the programme, which seeks to shift power not accuse the centre of exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative-led civic conservatism, which rests on a shared human nature and tradition.

public-service-media.rationale: The coalition kept the BBC and its licence-fee funding, and its open-services reform preserved public service media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not part of the programme; Big Society works through faith and community groups without taking a view on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the programme's free-market economics, which opens services to non-state providers and does not add farm price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The coalition kept the UK's nuclear deterrent (Trident); the programme itself does not address it.

workers-own-party.rationale: The programme gave community groups, not a workers' party, the role of representing citizens; inferred from its civic-conservative framing.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not part of the programme; inferred from British law, which the coalition left in place.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from British equality law, which the coalition kept; the programme did not address it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the programme's pro-civic-unity outlook and mainstream British views.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative-led coalition's use of regulation; the programme did not address it.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Britain has no customary chiefs; the programme devolves power to elected local bodies and communities.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Conservative-led coalition's market-friendly approach to environment policy.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from Conservative support for firm sentences; Big Society did not address it.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from Cameron's 2011 language requirement for migrants; the programme itself does not discuss it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not part of the programme; inferred from the Conservative-led coalition's preference for voluntary association over compulsion.

voter-id.rationale: Not part of the programme; inferred from the Conservative side's concern over electoral fraud and the coalition's registration reforms.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Cameron's emphasis on faith groups as civic partners in a plural society, with no single interpretation privileged.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from a liberal-democratic coalition that framed its reforms as returning power to citizens within the existing electoral system.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream British Conservative and Liberal Democrat opinion in 2010.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the programme's open-government and civil-liberties framing.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the coalition's welfare reform, which combined benefits into a payment that tapers with earnings, though this was not part of Big Society itself.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights for women were settled and uncontested in British politics by 2010, so adherents would agree strongly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the programme's reliance on faith groups and religious charities as engines of community action.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mainstream scholarly view held by the coalition's leaders.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the coalition's retention of the Government Equalities Office and its mainstream equality stance.

missingStatements.text: Citizens and community groups should have a legal right to take over local public assets and bid to run local services.
missingStatements.rationale: The community right to buy and right to bid were core launch policies enacted in the Localism Act 2011.

missingStatements.text: Young people should be encouraged to take part in a voluntary national service programme.
missingStatements.rationale: The National Citizen Service for 16- and 17-year-olds was a flagship Big Society initiative.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow UK policy detail (a specific youth programme); the lean bank does not need it.

missingStatements.text: Social investment from banks and dormant accounts should fund charities and social enterprises.
missingStatements.rationale: Big Society Capital was launched in 2011 with bank money and dormant account funds.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow UK policy detail (a specific funding vehicle); not a contested axis other ideologies would split on.

notes: Contested whether the programme was a distinct ideology or cover for austerity; Rees and Needham and Kisby argue ideas and recession interacted. Most of the 412 answers are inferred and low confidence.
